sentences.text: Pellegrinisaurus was a massive titanosaur, a type of giant sauropod dinosaur, estimated to reach lengths between 20 and 25 meters and weigh approximately 50 metric tons.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes an incomplete right femur, twenty-six caudal vertebrae, and four dorsal vertebrae.
Salgado interpreted the unique tail spine structure as an extra-articulation that reduced tail movement.
The preserved right femur is anteroposteriorly compressed with a very flattened fourth trochanter.
The holotype was found in the Allen Formation in Argentina in 1975 by Roberto Abel and his assistant Jaime Emilio Powell.
Researchers initially referred the remains to Epachthosaurus, but later abandoned this hypothesis because the specimen did not share derived features with the Epachthosaurus holotype.
Alamosaurus and Pellegrinisaurus have been considered possible members of Saltasaurinae, a classification originally proposed by Salgado for Pellegrinisaurus.
Pellegrinisaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Salgado suggested that larger titanosaurs like Pellegrinisaurus and theropods inhabited interior environments, while smaller titanosaurs and hadrosaurids lived in coastal lowlands.
